Context rot: recall degrades as tokens grow
claim: Context is a finite resource with diminishing marginal returns; as the number of tokens in the context window increases, a model's ability to accurately recall information from that context decreases ('context rot'), across all models.
evidence: S001: 'as the number of tokens in the context window increases, the model's ability to accurately recall information from that context decreases'; characteristic 'emerges across all models'.
relevance: Primary justification for keeping the active implementation context lean rather than appending an ever-growing transcript.

title: Attention budget and n-squared attention
claim: LLMs have a finite 'attention budget'; transformer attention creates n-squared pairwise relationships that get stretched thin as context grows, producing a performance gradient (reduced precision for retrieval and long-range reasoning) rather than a hard cliff.
evidence: S001: 'LLMs have an attention budget'; 'n^2 pairwise relationships for n tokens'; 'a performance gradient rather than a hard cliff'.
relevance: Explains why a single focused coding loop with curated context beats a polluted append-only log even below the hard limit.

title: Goal of context engineering: smallest high-signal token set
claim: Good context engineering means finding the smallest possible set of high-signal tokens that maximize the likelihood of the desired outcome.
evidence: S001: 'finding the smallest possible set of high-signal tokens that maximize the likelihood of some desired outcome'.
relevance: Design north-star for the proposed state artifacts and compaction outputs.

title: Three long-horizon techniques per Anthropic
claim: For long-horizon tasks Anthropic identifies three techniques to address context pollution: compaction, structured note-taking (agentic memory), and sub-agent architectures.
evidence: S001 section 'Context engineering for long-horizon tasks': 'compaction, structured note-taking, and multi-agent architectures'.
relevance: The proposal adopts the first two (compaction + note-taking/persisted state) for the single writer and narrows sub-agents to read-only roles.

title: Compaction summarizes and reinitiates, keeping decisions
claim: Compaction takes a conversation nearing the limit, summarizes it, and reinitiates a new window with the summary, preserving architectural decisions, unresolved bugs, and implementation details while discarding redundant tool outputs; Claude Code continues with the summary plus the five most recently accessed files.
evidence: S001: 'preserves architectural decisions, unresolved bugs, and implementation details while discarding redundant tool outputs'; 'continue with this compressed context plus the five most recently accessed files'.
relevance: Validates milestone compaction that preserves decisions and re-opens recent files instead of trusting stale memory.

title: Structured note-taking / agentic memory
claim: Structured note-taking (agentic memory) has the agent regularly write notes persisted outside the context window (e.g. a to-do list or NOTES.md) that get pulled back later, providing persistent memory with minimal overhead and tracking progress across dozens of tool calls.
evidence: S001: 'agent regularly writes notes persisted to memory outside of the context window... pulled back into the context window at later times'; 'maintaining critical context and dependencies that would otherwise be lost across dozens of tool calls'.
relevance: Directly supports persisting session state to file (.cartographer/ artifacts).

title: Just-in-time context via lightweight identifiers
claim: Agents should maintain lightweight identifiers (file paths, queries, links) and load data into context at runtime, mirroring human cognition; this enables progressive disclosure and keeps the working set focused.
evidence: S001: 'maintain lightweight identifiers (file paths, stored queries, web links) and use these references to dynamically load data into context at runtime'; Claude Code uses glob/grep to retrieve files just-in-time, 'bypassing the issues of stale indexing'.
relevance: Supports the state-refresh loop that re-opens relevant files from disk before editing rather than relying on memory.

title: Tool-result clearing is the lightest-touch compaction
claim: Clearing tool calls/results once they are deep in history is one of the safest, lightest-touch forms of compaction, and is a first-class strategy alongside compaction and memory.
evidence: S001: 'One of the safest lightest touch forms of compaction is tool result clearing'; launched as a Claude Developer Platform feature.
relevance: Supports tiered retention that summarizes/links bulky logs and tool output rather than retaining them verbatim.

title: Sub-agents are best for isolated read-only exploration
claim: Sub-agent architectures let specialized sub-agents explore extensively (tens of thousands of tokens) and return a condensed 1,000-2,000 token summary, keeping detailed search context isolated; this pattern shows substantial improvement on complex research/parallel exploration tasks.
evidence: S001: 'Each subagent might explore extensively... but returns only a condensed, distilled summary of its work (often 1,000-2,000 tokens)'; 'Multi-agent architectures handle complex research and analysis where parallel exploration pays dividends'.
relevance: Justifies retaining read-only specialist sub-agents (archivist/auditor/compass) while removing the writer sub-agent.

title: Technique choice depends on task characteristics
claim: The choice among compaction, note-taking, and multi-agent depends on the task: compaction for extensive back-and-forth, note-taking for iterative development with clear milestones, multi-agent for complex parallel research.
evidence: S001: 'Note-taking excels for iterative development with clear milestones; Multi-agent architectures handle complex research and analysis where parallel exploration pays dividends'.
relevance: Iterative phase-by-phase implementation with clear milestones is exactly the note-taking + compaction sweet spot, not the multi-writer-agent sweet spot.

title: Three composable primitives and what each operates on
claim: Compaction (whole-transcript, lossy summary, addresses all in-session growth), tool-result clearing (sub-transcript, drops re-fetchable results, lossless if re-callable, no inference cost), and memory (external storage, cross-session persistence) target different slices of the context problem and compose rather than compete.
evidence: S002 summary table: compaction 'whole conversation', clearing 'tool results in the current window', memory 'external storage, across windows'.
relevance: Gives a precise vocabulary for the proposed loop: clearing+compaction for in-session, persisted state files for cross-session/-compaction.

title: Compaction preserves high-level facts, loses obscure specifics
claim: Empirically compaction preserved 3/3 high-level task facts but 0/3 obscure appendix specifics; it keeps substance in compressed form but loses verbatim detail, and custom 'instructions' completely replace the default summarization prompt.
evidence: S002: 'RESULT: high-level 3/3 preserved, obscure 0/3 preserved'; 'custom instructions don't supplement this prompt — they completely replace it'.
relevance: Justifies a factual, hostile-to-ambiguity compaction artifact that explicitly enumerates exact paths/symbols/commands so critical specifics are not summarized away.

title: Tool-result clearing: bounded window, re-fetch tradeoff
claim: Tool-result clearing keeps the tool_use record but replaces the bulky result with a placeholder, bounding the window at no inference cost; the tradeoff is the agent may need to re-fetch cleared content, which is cheap for local files and costly for slow/ephemeral APIs.
evidence: S002: 'cheapest of the three primitives: no inference cost'; 'If the agent does need the data, it just calls the tool again'; cost 'depends on your tools'.
relevance: Supports keeping raw logs/diffs out of context and re-reading files on demand during the state-refresh loop.

title: Memory tool is model-driven with check-memory-first protocol
claim: The memory tool exposes file operations (view/create/str_replace/insert/delete/rename) the model drives itself; an auto-injected protocol instructs 'ALWAYS VIEW YOUR MEMORY DIRECTORY BEFORE DOING ANYTHING ELSE... Your context window might be reset at any moment'. With memory, Session 2 read 4 source files vs 8 without.
evidence: S002 Memory section: auto-injected 'check-memory-first protocol and an assume-interruption mindset'; 'Without memory: 8 file reads... With memory: 4 file reads'.
relevance: Directly models the proposed resumption prompt and the assume-interruption mindset for a single writer that may be compacted at any time.

title: Memory is only as good as what the agent saves
claim: Memory provides lossless persistence on whatever the agent chose to save, but its value depends entirely on the agent's judgment; sparse or poorly organized notes force a fallback to re-reading source documents.
evidence: S002: 'Memory's value depends on the agent's judgment about what to write'; 'If Session 1 had saved sparse or poorly organized notes, Session 2 would fall back to re-reading source documents'.
relevance: Motivates strict schemas and a compaction-as-validation step so persisted state is reliably useful.

title: Initializer-session structure for multi-session work
claim: For multi-session work, a dedicated first session should set up memory artifacts (progress log, feature checklist, references to setup scripts) so later sessions open by reading those artifacts to recover state instead of each inventing its own organization.
evidence: S002 'Implementing memory effectively': 'running a dedicated first session that sets up memory artifacts before substantive work begins... Subsequent sessions open by reading those artifacts to recover state'.
relevance: Supports an initialization step that scaffolds mission/plan/state/decisions/validation/working-set files before the implementation loop runs.

title: Context rot and latency scale with window contents, not the limit
claim: Even on 1M-token windows, the working set fills with stale tool results as fast as on 200K; context rot and prefill latency scale with how much is in the window, not with the window's limit, so keeping the working set lean is worthwhile regardless of window size.
evidence: S002: 'Context rot and prefill latency scale with how much is in the window, not with the window's limit, so keeping the working set lean is still worth doing even when the hard wall is far away.'
relevance: Counters the 'just wait for bigger context windows' objection; the loop is valuable on large-context models too.

title: Pick the primitive that matches the bottleneck
claim: Not every workload needs every primitive; skip memory for fresh independent sessions, skip compaction when sessions stay under the window, skip clearing when the agent needs full past tool results; the useful question is which problem the workload actually has.
evidence: S002 'When you might NOT want a primitive' and 'which of the three problems does my workload actually have?'.
relevance: Keeps the proposal minimal and tuned rather than bolting on all machinery indiscriminately.

title: Programmatic tool calling and tool search are adjacent levers
claim: Programmatic tool calling (running tools inside a model-authored program) keeps large results out of context entirely, and tool search trims tool-definition bloat; both are adjacent approaches to the tool-bloat problem.
evidence: S002 'Adjacent features': 'Programmatic tool calling (PTC) prevents large results from entering context at all'; 'Tool search trims tool-definition bloat'.
relevance: Notes future levers beyond the proposal's scope but consistent with its direction.

title: Two complementary memory systems in Claude Code
claim: Claude Code uses two complementary memory systems loaded every session: CLAUDE.md (user-written instructions/rules) and auto memory (learnings/patterns Claude writes itself); both are treated as context, not enforced configuration.
evidence: S003: 'CLAUDE.md files: instructions you write'; 'Auto memory: notes Claude writes itself'; 'Claude treats them as context, not enforced configuration'.
relevance: Maps onto the proposal's split between durable repo contract (AGENTS.md) and model-written rolling state (.cartographer/ files).

title: Concise specific memory is followed more reliably
claim: Because memory files are context rather than enforced configuration, concise and specific instructions are followed more reliably; CLAUDE.md should target under 200 lines, and vague or conflicting instructions reduce adherence (Claude may pick one arbitrarily).
evidence: S003: 'target under 200 lines'; 'if two rules contradict each other, Claude may pick one arbitrarily'; 'The more specific and concise your instructions, the more consistently Claude follows them'.
relevance: Justifies the rule that state artifacts be boring, structured, and hostile to ambiguity, and that AGENTS.md stay small.

title: Verifiable specificity over vague guidance
claim: Effective instructions are concrete enough to verify: 'Use 2-space indentation' beats 'format code properly'; 'Run npm test before committing' beats 'test your changes'.
evidence: S003 'Write effective instructions' examples.
relevance: Directly supports the brief's rule that checklists and next-actions be executable and unambiguous, not narrative.

title: Project-root memory survives compaction; chat-only instructions do not
claim: Project-root CLAUDE.md survives compaction because it is re-read from disk and re-injected after compaction, whereas instructions given only in conversation are lost after compaction unless written to a memory file.
evidence: S003 'Instructions seem lost after /compact': 'Project-root CLAUDE.md survives compaction... re-reads it from disk and re-injects it'; 'Add conversation-only instructions to CLAUDE.md to make them persist'.
relevance: Core mechanism behind 'persist state to file': only file-backed state reliably survives compaction/session resets.

title: Durable contract vs transient state; bounded memory load
claim: Memory is best split into durable repo contract vs transient task state; the auto-memory MEMORY.md index loads only the first 200 lines / 25KB at session start while topic files load on demand.
evidence: S003: CLAUDE.md vs auto memory table; 'first 200 lines of MEMORY.md, or the first 25KB... loaded at the start of every conversation'; 'Topic files... are not loaded at startup'.
relevance: Supports splitting one giant plan into a small always-loaded index plus on-demand detail files.

title: Use hooks, not memory text, for hard gates
claim: Memory/instruction files shape behavior but are not a hard enforcement layer; to block an action regardless of what the model decides, use a PreToolUse hook.
evidence: S003: 'To block an action regardless of what Claude decides, use a PreToolUse hook instead'; 'CLAUDE.md instructions shape Claude's behavior but are not a hard enforcement layer'.
relevance: Important risk caveat: deterministic validation/compaction-checks must be enforced by tooling, not just by prompt instructions.

title: Append-only/passive compression causes drift in SWE-agents
claim: Most existing SWE-agents rely on append-only context maintenance or passively triggered compression heuristics, which often lead to context explosion, semantic drift, and degraded reasoning in long-running interactions.
evidence: S004 abstract: 'append-only context maintenance or passively triggered compression heuristics, which often lead to context explosion, semantic drift, and degraded reasoning in long-running interactions'.
relevance: Peer-reviewed framing of the exact failure mode the proposal targets for coding agents specifically.

title: CAT makes context maintenance a callable tool with structured workspace
claim: CAT (Context as a Tool) elevates context maintenance to a callable tool integrated into the agent's decision-making, formalizing a structured context workspace of stable task semantics + condensed long-term memory + high-fidelity short-term interactions, and proactively compresses trajectories into actionable summaries at appropriate milestones.
evidence: S004 abstract: 'structured context workspace consisting of stable task semantics, condensed long-term memory, and high-fidelity short-term interactions... proactively compress historical trajectories into actionable summaries at appropriate milestones'.
relevance: Independent confirmation of the brief's milestone-driven compaction and four-layer state model (mission/plan/ground-truth/scratch).

title: Proactive compaction outperforms ReAct and static baselines on SWE-Bench
claim: SWE-Compressor (trained for CAT-style context management) reaches a 57.6% solved rate on SWE-Bench-Verified, significantly outperforming ReAct-based agents and static compression baselines while maintaining stable, scalable long-horizon reasoning under a bounded context budget.
evidence: S004 abstract: '57.6% solved rate and significantly outperforms ReAct-based agents and static compression baselines, while maintaining stable and scalable long-horizon reasoning under a bounded context budget'.
relevance: Quantitative evidence that proactive, milestone-driven context management improves coding-task success, not just efficiency.

title: The fundamental context-management trade-off
claim: ReAct-based agents suffer context saturation from accumulating noisy raw histories, while fixed full-history summarization risks irreversible loss of critical details; long-horizon effectiveness is hindered by this trade-off.
evidence: S005 abstract: 'Prevailing ReAct-based agents suffer from context saturation as they accumulate noisy, raw histories, while methods that fixedly summarize the full history at each step risk the irreversible loss of critical details'.
relevance: Names both failure poles the proposal must avoid: neither raw append-only nor naive full-history summarization.

title: AgentFold: multi-scale proactive folding of a cognitive workspace
claim: AgentFold treats context as a dynamic cognitive workspace to be actively sculpted rather than a passive log, performing a learned 'folding' operation at multiple scales each step: granular condensations preserve vital fine-grained details, deep consolidations abstract away entire multi-step sub-tasks.
evidence: S005 abstract: 'dynamic cognitive workspace to be actively sculpted... folding operation, which manages its historical trajectory at multiple scales: granular condensations to preserve vital, fine-grained details, or deep consolidations to abstract away entire multi-step sub-tasks'.
relevance: Direct support for tiered retention: keep exact details where needed, deeply consolidate completed phases to 'done + evidence'.

title: Folding lets small models beat much larger ones
claim: With simple supervised fine-tuning, AgentFold-30B-A3B achieves 36.2% on BrowseComp and 47.3% on BrowseComp-ZH, surpassing or matching dramatically larger open models (e.g. DeepSeek-V3.1-671B-A37B) and leading proprietary agents like OpenAI's o4-mini.
evidence: S005 abstract: '36.2% on BrowseComp and 47.3% on BrowseComp-ZH... surpasses or matches open-source models of a dramatically larger scale... but also surpasses leading proprietary agents like OpenAI's o4-mini'.
relevance: Evidence that disciplined context folding is a high-leverage lever, plausibly more impactful than raw scale or more agents.

title: The core problem is a polluted append-only event log
claim: The core problem is not merely a small context window but that context becomes a polluted append-only event log: the agent keeps seeing obsolete hypotheses, dead-end tool output, stale plans, verbose diffs, and one-off reasoning that should no longer influence behavior.
evidence: S006: 'the context becomes a polluted append-only event log. The agent keeps seeing obsolete hypotheses, dead-end tool output, stale plans, verbose diffs, and one-off reasoning that should no longer influence behavior.'
relevance: States the problem the proposal solves, consistent with F026/F029.

title: Four-layer working memory; only three survive compaction
claim: Long-horizon state should split into four layers: Mission (goal, non-goals, acceptance criteria), Plan (current phase, ordered tasks, status, blockers), Ground truth (files changed, decisions, APIs/contracts, passing/failing commands), and Scratch (recent tool calls, exploration, failed attempts, noisy logs). Only the first three should survive compaction; scratch is aggressively discarded or summarized.
evidence: S006 'maintain a working memory, not a transcript': enumerated Mission/Plan/Ground truth/Scratch; 'Only the first three should survive compaction. The fourth should be aggressively discarded or summarized.'
relevance: Defines the artifact layering the proposal implements; mirrors CAT's stable/long-term/short-term split (F027).

title: Harnesses fail by compacting conversation, not project state
claim: Most agent harnesses fail because they compact the conversation rather than the project state, which preserves the wrong thing.
evidence: S006: 'Most agent harnesses fail because they compact the conversation, not the project state. That preserves the wrong thing.'
relevance: Key insight: persist and compact structured project state to file rather than relying on conversational compaction alone.

title: Compaction should be milestone-driven, an explicit workflow action
claim: Auto-compaction near the limit is too late (the agent is already degraded); compaction should fire after each semantic milestone (proposal accepted, phase started, phase completed, test failure diagnosed, architectural decision made, file set changes, before switching areas, before a risky refactor) as an explicit action, not a last-resort cleanup.
evidence: S006 'Tactical compaction should be milestone-driven, not emergency-driven' with the enumerated milestone list; 'compaction should be an explicit action in the workflow, not a last-resort cleanup.'
relevance: Defines the proposed compaction trigger policy; matches CAT's milestone compaction (F027).

title: Keep compaction factual, not narrative
claim: A compaction artifact must be boring, structured, and hostile to ambiguity, preserving exact file paths, symbols, commands, failing assertions, decisions, the single next action, and explicit non-goals; it must not preserve prior speculation, long logs, repeated explanations, abandoned approaches, raw tool output, 'we might' language, or emotional status like 'almost done'.
evidence: S006 'Keep compaction factual, not narrative': preserve list vs. should-not-preserve list.
relevance: Defines the content contract for the state/compaction artifact; complements F012 (compaction loses obscure specifics unless named).

title: Split memory into typed artifacts, not one giant file
claim: One giant PLAN.md eventually becomes the same problem as a giant context window, so state should be split into separate artifacts: mission.md (stable goal/criteria/non-goals), plan.md (phase/task checklist), state.md (compacted live working memory), decisions.md (append-only ADR-lite), validation.md (commands, last result, known failures), working-set.md (relevant files/symbols), and handoff.md (generated before compaction/restart).
evidence: S006 'Use different artifacts for different memory types' with the .cartographer/ file listing.
relevance: Specifies the concrete on-disk artifact set the proposal adds.

title: State-refresh loop before every major edit
claim: Before a major edit the agent should: read state.md, read working-set.md, re-open only the relevant files, restate the next action in one sentence, edit, run targeted validation, then update state.md; do not rely on the model remembering code it read 40 turns ago.
evidence: S006 'Use state refresh before every major edit': numbered loop; 'do not rely on the model remembering code it read 40 turns ago. Make it re-open the relevant files. Context memory is not a database.'
relevance: Defines the per-edit discipline that replaces trusting stale in-context memory; aligns with just-in-time retrieval (F007).

title: Store decisions separately from tasks (append-only)
claim: Decisions should be stored separately from tasks in an append-only ADR-lite decisions.md (each with reason and impact) because plans change constantly while decisions should not; this prevents the agent relitigating already-settled issues after compaction.
evidence: S006 'Store decisions separately from tasks' with D-001/D-002/D-003 examples; 'This prevents the agent from relitigating already-settled issues after compaction.'
relevance: Maps onto Cartographer's existing decision/ADR machinery and the proposal's decisions.md artifact.

title: Current working set as a cheap file-level lease
claim: The agent should maintain a working set file listing Active (editing now), Relevant-but-not-active, and Out-of-scope files, and must not edit files outside Active unless it first updates the working-set file with a reason — a cheap file-level lease system for a single agent.
evidence: S006 'Use current working set aggressively'; 'Do not edit files outside Active unless you first update working-set.md with a reason. This is basically a cheap file-level lease system for a single agent.'
relevance: Provides scope control for the single writer that previously came from pathfinder's allowed-files contract.

title: Tiered retention by context type
claim: Retention should be tiered: keep mission/acceptance and decisions verbatim (append-only), keep current phase compact-but-exact, keep file paths/symbols and failing commands/assertions exact, summarize logs with a link/path to the raw artifact, drop exploration unless it changed a decision, keep failed attempts only if likely retried accidentally, and collapse old completed phases to 'done + evidence'.
evidence: S006 'Don't compact everything equally' tiered retention table; aligns with AgentFold multi-scale folding.
relevance: Operationalizes F030 (granular vs deep folding) into a concrete retention policy.

title: Add an explicit forget/ignore list
claim: A 'forget/ignore' list should explicitly record stale ideas, replaced designs, and obsolete failures to prevent the agent resurrecting them after compaction, because summaries that say 'we considered X' without 'do not do X' invite stale-idea resurrection.
evidence: S006 'Add a forget list': examples ('Ignore earlier idea to use fast-glob'); 'Agents often resurrect stale ideas after compaction because the summary says we considered X without saying do not do X.'
relevance: A small, high-leverage addition to the state schema that compaction validation can enforce.

title: Keep raw evidence outside the main context
claim: Raw logs should live in files (e.g. .logs/2026-...-test-fail.txt) and validation.md should reference the command, the raw-log path, and the relevant error, so the agent can reopen the raw log only when needed instead of pasting logs into chat or the state file.
evidence: S006 'Keep raw evidence outside the main context'; ties to tool-result clearing/context editing where 'the useful fact survives, the bulky tool output does not.'
relevance: Aligns with Cartographer's existing Clean Context Contract (raw output to /tmp, compact receipts).

title: Checklists are executable control flow, not documentation
claim: Checklists should be executable by the agent (concrete tasks and commands) rather than vague documentation; avoid items like 'improve parser', 'clean up tests', or 'make sure everything works' because they invite sloppy behavior.
evidence: S006 'Use checklists as control flow, not documentation' with good/bad examples.
relevance: Reinforces verifiable specificity (F022) for the plan/checklist artifact.

title: Force a single next action per snapshot
claim: Every state snapshot should end with exactly one next action; multiple next actions increase the chance the agent picks the wrong one after compaction.
evidence: S006 'Force next action to be singular' with single-vs-multiple examples.
relevance: A concrete invariant the compaction-validation step can check.

title: Compaction triggers for the harness; 60% is a heuristic
claim: Explicit harness compaction triggers should include context usage above ~60%, phase boundaries, more than N files inspected, more than N tool calls since last state update, after any failed validation diagnosis, before a broad refactor, and before handing off to another session; the 60% threshold is third-party Claude Code guidance, not official Anthropic, so treat it as a heuristic.
evidence: S006 'Add compaction triggers to the harness'; 'The 60% threshold appears in third-party Claude Code guidance, not official Anthropic docs, so I would treat it as a heuristic rather than a rule.'
relevance: Defines configurable trigger policy with an explicit caveat to avoid over-stating the source.

title: Make compaction itself a validation step
claim: After producing a compacted state the agent should verify it against the repo/artifacts: confirm active files exist, confirm current failing/passing commands are recorded, confirm the next action maps to an unchecked plan item, and confirm no completed item is still listed as active — because a bad summary is worse than no summary once future work treats it as canonical.
evidence: S006 'Make compaction a validation step'; 'A bad summary is worse than no summary because future work treats it as canonical.'
relevance: Defines the verification gate for compaction outputs; complements F015 (memory only as good as what is saved).

title: Rolling state beats summary-of-chat
claim: A continuously updated rolling state file beats a chat summary generated only when context is already large, because each rolling update happens while the relevant facts are fresh; compaction then just discards the transcript and reloads the artifacts.
evidence: S006 'Prefer rolling state over summary of chat'; 'Discard prior transcript. Reload mission.md, plan.md, state.md, decisions.md, validation.md, and working-set.md.'
relevance: Core design principle: update state after every material action rather than summarizing at the cliff.

title: Phase receipt as structured source of truth
claim: After each completed chunk the agent should emit a structured phase receipt (phase, status, changed_files, decisions, validation commands+status, next_phase) so future compaction has a structured source of truth instead of prose.
evidence: S006 'Add a phase receipt after each completed chunk' with the JSON example.
relevance: Cartographer already has receipts.jsonl/validation_runner.py; the proposal extends them as the canonical compaction source.

title: Fixed resumption prompt after compaction/restart
claim: After compaction or a new session, use a fixed resumption prompt that resumes from repository artifacts (read mission, decisions, plan, state, working-set, validation in order) and requires the agent to respond with current phase, next single action, and files to inspect before editing — and not to edit until after that response.
evidence: S006 'Use resumption prompts' with the ordered read list and 'Do not edit until after that response.'
relevance: Operationalizes the assume-interruption mindset (F014) as a concrete guardrail against post-compaction amnesia.

title: AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md hold stable rules, not live task state
claim: Project instruction files should contain stable operating rules (test commands, commit policy, 'update state.md after material changes') and must not contain live task state like 'currently debugging route parser empty segment test'.
evidence: S006 'Avoid overloading CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md' good-vs-bad contents; aligns with F020/F024.
relevance: Keeps the durable repo contract separate from transient rolling state, preventing AGENTS.md bloat.

title: The long-horizon parent loop replacing writer subagents
claim: The proposed long-horizon loop is: Orient (read mission/plan/state/decisions/validation) -> Select (one next action) -> Narrow (update working set) -> Inspect (re-open files from disk) -> Act (small patch) -> Validate (narrowest useful command) -> Record (update state/validation/receipts) -> Compact (if trigger fires, rewrite state/handoff and clear transcript noise) -> Continue (re-orient from artifacts). This loop is the long-horizon replacement for writer subagents.
evidence: S006 'A strong long-horizon loop for Pi-Cartographer' numbered steps; 'This is the long-horizon replacement for writer subagents.'
relevance: The central design the proposal implements in the implement skill.

title: Proposed cartographer-compact mode with schema checks
claim: The brief proposes a cartographer-compact command/mode that generates state.md, working-set.md, validation.md, and handoff.md with checks: no vague next action, no missing active files, no stale failed command if a later passing receipt exists, no out-of-scope files in the working set, every current task maps to a plan item, and every decision has date/source/impact; after compaction the agent must reload artifacts and ignore prior chat except the latest user instruction.
evidence: S006 'What I would add to Pi-Cartographer'; the cartographer-compact schema and hard instruction.
relevance: Concrete tooling proposal: a deterministic compaction/validation helper analogous to validation_runner.py.

title: Reframe: externalize state, do not offload edits
claim: The better abstraction is not 'offload the edit work to save context' but 'externalize durable task state so the same editor can survive context churn'; subagents save context by moving work elsewhere, while tactical compaction saves context by making the important state non-conversational.
evidence: S006 'The main correction to your current framing': '...externalize durable task state so the same editor can survive context churn.'
relevance: States the thesis for sunsetting the writer subagent in favor of in-place context engineering.

title: Recommended stack for now: single writer + state + read-only specialists
claim: For now the best stack is a single writer agent plus explicit plan/proposal artifacts, a rolling state snapshot, phase receipts, a decision log, a working-set file, a validation log, proactive compaction, and read-only specialist agents only; this addresses the 'agent gets sloppy, then compacted, then lobotomized' failure mode better than parallel writer agents.
evidence: S006 closing: enumerated stack; 'That should address the agent gets sloppy, then compacted, then lobotomized failure mode better than parallel writer agents.'
relevance: Defines the end-state architecture: keep read-only specialists, remove the writer subagent.

title: cartographer-pathfinder is the single-phase writer subagent
claim: cartographer-pathfinder is a narrow single-phase implementation worker (tools: read, bash, edit, write, plus read-only cartographer helpers) that implements one approved plan phase from a context pack and must not commit, stage, append canonical receipts, write ADRs, or read raw private inputs.
evidence: S015 (.pi/agents/cartographer-pathfinder.md): 'narrow Pi Cartographer implementation agent... implement one approved plan phase'; 'Do not commit, stage files, append canonical receipts, write ADRs, or read raw private inputs.'
relevance: Defines exactly the agent being sunset and the duties that must move to the single parent writer.

title: implement skill delegates phase edits to pathfinder by default
claim: The implement skill executes a plan phase-by-phase and delegates actual phase edits to cartographer-pathfinder as the default phase writer (built-in worker is an approved fallback only), while the parent owns sequencing, quality gates, checklist updates, commits, and final reporting.
evidence: S010 (skills/implement/SKILL.md): 'delegates... actual phase edits/fixes to cartographer-pathfinder as the default phase writer; built-in worker is an approved fallback only.'
relevance: This is the workflow that the proposal rewrites to a single-writer context-engineering loop.

title: ADR-0002 made delegated writer work provisional
claim: ADR-0002 (accepted 2026-06-08) requires Cartographer to treat delegated subagent work as provisional until parent-owned deterministic validation receipts and a read-only cartographer-auditor PASS exist, with least-privilege helper access, structured acceptance contracts, bounded timeout/control handling, and sanitized evidence boundaries.
evidence: S012 (ADR-0002 Decision): 'treat delegated subagent work as provisional until parent-owned deterministic validation receipts and a read-only cartographer-auditor PASS exist...'.
relevance: The proposal narrows the writer-subagent portion of ADR-0002; it must amend/supersede that decision rather than silently contradict it.

title: Session evidence: workers left the parent to finish implementation
claim: The subagent-reliability proposal's sanitized session evidence counted 107 subagent calls, 17 subagent errors, longest subagent turns around 600s/566s/300s, 2,035 entries, four compactions, and tool/text outputs up to 166,878 characters, and the user reported that worker agents left the parent to finish implementation.
evidence: S013 (subagent-reliability proposal Problem Statement table): '107 subagent calls, 17 subagent errors... longest subagent turns of about 600s, 566s, and 300s'; '2,035 entries, four compactions, and tool/text outputs up to 166,878 characters'; 'worker agents left the parent to finish implementation.'
relevance: Empirical, in-repo motivation that a writer subagent did not reliably reduce parent work and added latency/errors.

title: Cartographer already has persisted-state machinery
claim: Cartographer already persists workflow state in small JSONL records (.plan/<topic>/receipts.jsonl and context-packs.jsonl), enforces a Clean Context Contract (~8KB normal / ~16KB diagnostic budgets, raw output to /tmp, compact receipts), and ships analyze_session.py and validation_runner.py for session telemetry and deterministic validation receipts.
evidence: S011 (README Clean Context Contract + 'What gets written'): receipts.jsonl/context-packs.jsonl, 8KB/16KB budgets, '/tmp/pi-cartographer-runs/'; S016 (analyze_session.py, validation_runner.py).
relevance: The proposal extends existing infrastructure rather than inventing it; lowers implementation cost and risk.

title: Single-writer-per-worktree safety is already project policy
claim: Cartographer policy already requires one writer per worktree and notes that 'async does not make parallel writes safe' and writers should not modify the same active worktree unless deliberately isolated; the git-worktrees proposal codifies one topic -> one branch -> one worktree.
evidence: S014 (git-worktrees proposal): 'preserving one writer per worktree'; 'async does not make parallel writes safe, and writers should not modify the same active worktree unless they are deliberately isolated.'
relevance: Supports D-001 in the brief (no writer subagents for now due to merge/worktree safety) and the single-writer end-state.

title: Read-only Cartographer specialists already add judgment
claim: Cartographer already defines read-only specialist agents that add judgment without writing source: cartographer-archivist (research compression), cartographer-auditor (semantic gate after deterministic receipts), cartographer-compass (scope/dependency/repeated-failure decisions), cartographer-drafter (artifact drafting), and cartographer-redactor (private-artifact sanitization).
evidence: S011 (README Cartographer subagents table) and subagent list; auditor 'Performs semantic review after deterministic validation receipts pass.'
relevance: These map exactly onto Anthropic's recommended read-only sub-agent pattern (F009) and are retained by the proposal.

title: Anthropic server-side compaction (compact_20260112)
claim: First-party compaction context edit: triggers at a token threshold (default 150K, min 50K), returns a typed compaction content block, supports custom 'instructions' (which fully replace the default summarization prompt) and pause_after_compaction.
evidence: S002 tactical table and 'Using the API'; default prompt quoted verbatim in the cookbook.
relevance: Reference implementation for milestone/threshold compaction; Pi/Cartographer can mirror its trigger+instructions design.

title: Anthropic tool-result clearing (clear_tool_uses_20250919)
claim: First-party context edit that clears old tool_result blocks server-side: default trigger 100K, keep default 3 tool uses, with clear_at_least, exclude_tools, and clear_tool_inputs; exclude_tools:[memory] is recommended when combined with the memory tool.
evidence: S002 tactical table, clearing section, and 'Note on exclude_tools'.
relevance: Model for keeping bulky re-fetchable tool output out of the implementation loop's context.

title: Anthropic memory tool (memory_20250818)
claim: Client-side memory tool with view/create/str_replace/insert/delete/rename operations and an auto-injected check-memory-first protocol; the application implements the file backend, controlling what is stored and for how long.
evidence: S002 Memory section and tactical table.
relevance: Conceptual analog for the .cartographer/ persisted state files that the single writer reads/writes.

title: Compaction is lossy; a bad summary is canonical
claim: Compaction loses obscure but sometimes-critical specifics, and once persisted, a bad summary is treated as canonical truth by future work, which is worse than no summary.
evidence: S002 (3/3 high-level vs 0/3 obscure preserved); S006 'A bad summary is worse than no summary'.
relevance: Requires the compaction-as-validation gate (F047) and factual exact-detail content contract (F036).

title: Persisted state is only as good as what is written
claim: If the single writer records sparse, stale, or disorganized state, the loop degrades to re-reading sources or, worse, acting on wrong canonical state.
evidence: S002 'Memory's value depends on the agent's judgment'; S006 tiered-retention and validation guidance.
relevance: Mitigated by strict schemas, rolling updates after every material action (F048), and deterministic compaction checks (F053).

title: Prompt instructions are not hard enforcement
claim: State-refresh, working-set leasing, and compaction rules expressed only as instructions are context, not enforced configuration, so the model may not follow them reliably; hard gates need tooling/hooks.
evidence: S003 'use a PreToolUse hook instead'; 'instructions shape behavior but are not a hard enforcement layer'.
relevance: The proposal must back critical invariants with deterministic helpers/validation, not prompt text alone.

title: Loss of parallel write throughput
claim: A single writer cannot fan out parallel edits across many files/areas the way multiple writer subagents nominally could; throughput on embarrassingly-parallel edits may drop.
evidence: S001 multi-agent architectures 'handle complex research... where parallel exploration pays dividends'; offset by F063 showing writer handoffs added rework/latency in practice.
relevance: Bounded by keeping read-only parallel specialists and the git-worktrees model for genuinely independent topics.

title: Must reconcile with ADR-0002
claim: ADR-0002 assumes a delegated writer (pathfinder) exists; sunsetting it requires an explicit superseding/amending ADR so the documented decision record stays coherent.
evidence: S012 ADR-0002 Decision and 'How to Use This Decision' (applies when changing implementation/subagent workflows).
relevance: Drives the adr_required:true intent for this proposal.

title: State-file proliferation could recreate the giant-context problem
claim: Adding mission/plan/state/decisions/validation/working-set/handoff files could itself bloat into a giant always-loaded context if not tiered, size-capped, and compacted.
evidence: S006 'One giant PLAN.md eventually becomes the same problem as a giant context window'; S003 200-line/25KB load limits.
relevance: Mitigated by a small always-loaded index plus on-demand detail files and size budgets (F024, F037).

title: Honor the Clean Context Contract
claim: New state artifacts and any compaction helper must honor Cartographer's Clean Context Contract: ~8KB normal / ~16KB diagnostic LLM-facing budgets, raw output to /tmp/pi-cartographer-runs, and compact receipts for larger output.
evidence: S011 README Clean Context Contract.
relevance: Keeps the new loop consistent with existing tooling expectations.

title: Preserve serial/single-checkout and no-subagent operation
claim: The workflow must keep working when no subagents are available and in single-checkout mode; the change should make the single-writer path primary rather than forbidding fallbacks.
evidence: S013 subagent-reliability non-goals: 'Do not make subagents mandatory when no executable subagents are available; serial fallback should remain supported, explicit, and receipted.'
relevance: Sunsetting the writer subagent aligns with, and is easier under, existing serial-fallback support.

title: Do not require changes to the pi-subagents runtime
claim: The proposal should not require changing Pi's pi-subagents runtime or external orchestration frameworks; it should be implementable in Cartographer skills, agent definitions, docs, and helper scripts.
evidence: S013 subagent-reliability non-goals: 'Do not change Pi's pi-subagents runtime or require new external orchestration frameworks.'
relevance: Bounds scope to Cartographer-owned artifacts and keeps implementation low-risk.

title: Single-writer context-engineering loop
description: Replace the cartographer-pathfinder writer subagent with one focused writer (the parent) running the Orient->Select->Narrow->Inspect->Act->Validate->Record->Compact->Continue loop.

title: Strategic milestone-driven compaction
description: Make compaction an explicit, milestone-triggered workflow action with a factual, validated state artifact instead of emergency near-limit auto-compaction.

title: Persisted session state to file
description: Persist tiered, rolling working memory in typed .cartographer/ artifacts (mission/plan/state/decisions/validation/working-set/handoff) so the same editor survives context churn and session resets.

title: Reconcile with ADR-0002
description: Amend or supersede the writer-subagent portion of ADR-0002 with a new ADR so the decision record stays coherent.

title: Keep read-only specialists
description: Retain cartographer-auditor/compass/archivist as read-only specialists that explore/review in isolated context and return condensed results; only the writer subagent leaves the default path.

title: Reuse existing infrastructure
description: Build on existing receipts/context-packs, Clean Context Contract, validation_runner.py, and analyze_session.py rather than inventing parallel machinery.

title: User directive (session): agent state as JSON graph structures
Agent working state must be JSON/JSONL graph structures
claim: All agent working-memory/state must be strictly-structured JSON or JSONL graph structures (typed nodes + edges) referenceable by stable ID; working memory does not need to be human-readable. Human-readable artifacts (proposal, plan, ADRs, README) remain Markdown.
evidence: S007 (user directive): 'use json and jsonl files since they are more strictly structured and easier to reference by ID. The working memory doesn't need to be human readable. All agent state should be JSON graph structures, human readable artifacts should be markdown.'
relevance: Replaces the brief's seven Markdown state files with structured JSON/JSONL artifacts (not Markdown). Facts F070-F082 refine the initial 'typed nodes + edges' framing into the adopted model: a canonical state.json snapshot + append-only JSONL history + a plan.json task graph, validated by schemas/invariants and mutated via an ACI.

title: agent-state-data-shape.md (design conversation: state file formats)
agent-state-data-management.md (design conversation: ACI vs raw files)
SWE-agent: Agent-Computer Interfaces Enable Automated Software Engineering (arXiv 2405.15793, NeurIPS 2024)
publisher: Yang, Jimenez, Wettig, Lieret, Yao, Narasimhan, Press (Princeton)

title: Format-by-purpose: structured files for agent state, Markdown for humans
claim: For state the agent must repeatedly reload, update, diff, validate, and trust, use schema-constrained structured files, not Markdown. Format by purpose: human-facing docs = Markdown; current agent state = JSON; append-only history/receipts = JSONL; stable config/policy = TOML.
evidence: S008: 'for state the agent must repeatedly reload, update, diff, validate, and trust, use schema-constrained structured files'; table 'Human-facing docs: Markdown; Agent state snapshots: JSON; Append-only history: JSONL; Config/policy: TOML or YAML; Validation receipts: JSONL'.
relevance: Replaces the brief's Markdown state files with a precise format-by-purpose policy for the .cartographer/ state.

title: JSON is best for current state (one canonical, schema-validatable snapshot)
claim: Use JSON for the current state snapshot: one canonical snapshot that is schema-validatable, with exact keys that reduce drift, easy to diff/patch/parse, able to require next_action to be singular and to reject unknown fields. Verbosity is the cost and is acceptable for agent-only state.
evidence: S008 'JSON is best for current state': 'can be schema validated... exact keys reduce drift... can require next_action to be singular... can reject unknown fields'; 'JSON is verbose... acceptable for agent-only state'.
relevance: Defines state.json as the canonical current-truth snapshot rather than a Markdown or loose graph.

title: JSONL is best for receipts and event history
claim: Use JSONL for append-only logs (receipts, events): appends are simple, records are atomic, easy to audit/summarize, no merge conflicts across unrelated entries, streamable, and compactable into state.json. Use JSONL for history; use JSON for current truth.
evidence: S008 'JSONL is best for receipts and event history': bullet list; 'Use JSONL for history. Use JSON for current truth.'
relevance: Defines validation.jsonl/decisions.jsonl/events.jsonl as append-only history that compaction folds into state.json.

title: Avoid YAML for canonical agent state
claim: YAML is worse than it looks for agent-owned state: indentation-sensitive, implicit typing surprises, multiple equivalent representations, anchors/aliases add complexity, easier for LLMs to produce subtly invalid output, and harder to patch safely. Fine for human-owned config, not the canonical machine state format.
evidence: S008 'YAML is worse than it looks': problem list; 'I would not make it the canonical machine state format.'
relevance: Rules out YAML for state files; TOML is preferred for config.

title: TOML for stable config, not live state
claim: TOML is better than YAML for deterministic, human-edited, stable config with modest nesting (e.g. compaction triggers, per-agent mode/allowed-tools, pathfinder enabled=false); it is not ideal for frequently changing task state.
evidence: S008 'TOML is good for stable config, not live state': config.toml example with [compaction] and [agents.*]; 'not ideal for frequently changing task state'.
relevance: Defines config.toml for compaction policy and agent modes, separate from live state.

title: Demote Markdown to generated, non-authoritative views
claim: Markdown should be derived or human-facing, not canonical task state: JSON/JSONL are canonical and Markdown (e.g. status.md, validation.md) is rendered from them for humans. The agent must treat generated Markdown as non-authoritative (generated_views with authoritative:false) to avoid reading stale prose and ignoring structured state.
evidence: S008 'Markdown should be derived or human-facing': 'JSON/JSONL are canonical. Markdown is rendered from them for humans'; generated_views authoritative:false; 'prevents... agent reads stale prose and ignores the structured state.'
relevance: Resolves the human-readability concern without making Markdown canonical; status.md is a generated view.

title: Canonical state + rendered views architecture
claim: Best architecture: a canonical current-state file (state.json) plus a canonical append-only event stream (events.jsonl), with generated Markdown (status.md) explicitly marked not a source of truth.
evidence: S008 'Best architecture: canonical state + rendered views': state.json canonical, events.jsonl canonical, status.md 'generated view, not source of truth'.
relevance: Two-tier model: machine truth in structured files, human understanding in generated Markdown.

title: Use schemas + invariants aggressively
claim: The real win is JSON + schema + invariants, not JSON alone. Keep schemas/{state,plan,working-set,validation,decision}.schema.json and enforce invariants: next_action required and singular; current_phase.id exists in plan.json; working-set.active files exist; forbidden paths may not overlap allowed write paths; validation receipt IDs unique; completed tasks may not also be active; unknown top-level fields rejected.
evidence: S008 'Use schemas aggressively': schema file list and invariant list; 'That is how you stop left up to whim in structure.'
relevance: Defines the deterministic checks the cartographer-compact/state-validate helper enforces (replacing prompt-only rules).

title: Keep state compact by design with explicit limits
claim: State must not become a transcript replacement; encode explicit limits (e.g. max_active_files, max_next_actions=1, max_known_failures, max_recent_events, max_summary_chars). Old detail belongs in JSONL receipts, logs, or phase summaries.
evidence: S008 'Keep state compact by design': limits object; 'Old detail belongs in JSONL receipts, logs, or phase summaries.'
relevance: Bounds state.json size, mitigating the state-file-proliferation/giant-context risk.

title: Suggested canonical machine-state file set
claim: Suggested canonical files: state.json (current truth: current_phase_id, focus, next_action_id, active_task_ids, blocked, known_failures, last_validation_receipt_id), plan.json (phases->tasks with id/status/depends_on), working-set.json (mode + active/read_only/forbidden with reasons), validation.jsonl, decisions.jsonl, events.jsonl, and handoff.json (resume_order, resume_instruction, must_ignore).
evidence: S008 'Suggested canonical files' with concrete JSON examples for state.json/plan.json/working-set.json/validation.jsonl/decisions.jsonl/handoff.json.
relevance: Concrete artifact set replacing the brief's seven Markdown files.

title: Use enums, not natural-language status
claim: Do not use natural language where enums would work. Use enums: task/phase status pending|active|blocked|complete|cancelled|superseded; validation status unknown|passed|failed|skipped|waived; scope read_only|write_allowed|forbidden|generated|external.
evidence: S008 'Do not use natural language where enums would work': bad 'mostly done, but needs another look' vs good {status:blocked, blocker:test_failure}; enum lists.
relevance: Makes state machine-checkable and unambiguous; feeds schema validation.

title: Add stable IDs everywhere
claim: Agents are much less sloppy when they refer to stable IDs (phase_id, task_id, decision_id, validation_id, event_id, file_ref_id) instead of prose; this also makes compaction safer.
evidence: S008 'Add IDs everywhere': bad 'the parser task' vs good 'task_017'; 'This also makes compaction safer.'
relevance: All cross-file references (state->plan, state->validation, state->decisions) are by ID.

title: JSON Patch as a tool-level update primitive
claim: Updating state by rewriting the whole file risks dropping fields; a safer internal protocol applies JSON Patch ops (e.g. replace /current_phase_id) as a tool-level primitive, even if JSON Patch is not exposed to users.
evidence: S008 'JSON patching is useful': JSON Patch replace-op example; 'useful as a tool-level primitive.'
relevance: Informs how the state-mutation ACI applies partial, safe updates.

title: Hybrid: read state as files, mutate state through tools
claim: Do not choose between raw files and an ACI. Use a hybrid: canonical state in JSON/JSONL files, mutation through ACI commands, validation via JSON Schema + invariant checks, and human visibility via generated Markdown. The LLM reads state as files and changes state through tools, giving both observability and deterministic correctness.
evidence: S009: 'LLM reads state as files. LLM changes state through tools.'; 'Canonical state: JSON/JSONL files in repo; Mutation interface: ACI commands/tools; Validation: JSON Schema + invariant checks; Human visibility: Generated Markdown/status views.'
relevance: Defines the core read/write split for the proposed state system.

title: ACIs are safer for state mutation than direct JSON editing
claim: Direct LLM editing of canonical JSON has predictable failures (drops/invents fields, corrupts JSON, updates without appending a receipt, marks a task complete without validation, creates contradictory state, forgets cross-file invariants). A semantic ACI command (e.g. task complete --validation val_004) enforces preconditions and updates state.json/plan.json/events.jsonl together.
evidence: S009 'Why ACIs are better for state mutation': failure-mode list; 'cartographer task complete task_017 --validation val_004' enforcing existence/active/validation-passed/phase-membership/next-task/atomic multi-file update.
relevance: Justifies a mutation ACI rather than asking the single writer to hand-edit three JSON files correctly.

title: SWE-agent: a custom ACI materially improves agent performance
claim: The SWE-agent work argues that interface design materially affects agent performance and that agents benefit from purpose-built operations rather than raw low-level computer interaction; a custom Agent-Computer Interface improved agents' ability to navigate repositories, edit files, and run tests.
evidence: S009 references SWE-agent's ACI argument; S017 (SWE-agent: Agent-Computer Interfaces Enable Automated Software Engineering, arXiv 2405.15793, NeurIPS 2024) introduces the agent-computer-interface concept and reports improved navigation/editing/testing.
relevance: External, peer-reviewed support for adding a Cartographer state-management ACI.

title: Raw files remain essential for observability
claim: Do not hide all state behind an opaque ACI: raw JSON/JSONL files are visible, diffable, greppable, Git-friendly, PR-reviewable, recoverable, model-readable, and schema-validatable outside the harness. An ACI-only store makes tool output the only reality and makes bugs/recovery/auditing harder.
evidence: S009 'Why raw files are still important': failure-mode list and 'Raw JSON/JSONL files are valuable because they are: visible, diffable, greppable, Git-friendly...'.
relevance: Requires keeping the canonical state as inspectable files, not an opaque database.

title: Observable state, controlled writes (four paths)
claim: The ideal pattern separates four paths: read path (agent may read JSON/JSONL files directly), write path (agent uses ACI commands), validation path (ACI validates schema + invariants after every mutation), and audit path (ACI appends JSONL receipts/events).
evidence: S009 'Best architecture: observable state, controlled writes': Read/Write/Validation/Audit path definitions.
relevance: Defines the operational contract for the implement loop's Record/Validate steps.

title: ACIs should expose semantic transitions, not generic setters
claim: A weak ACI offers generic setters (set /current_phase_id P3), barely better than direct JSON editing; a strong ACI exposes semantic state transitions (phase advance --from P2 --to P3 --receipt phase_002) that enforce business rules. Good commands: task.start/block/complete, validation.record, decision.accept, working_set.claim/release, phase.advance, compact.generate, handoff.refresh. Design around transitions, not fields.
evidence: S009 'ACIs should expose semantic operations, not generic setters': weak vs strong examples and command list.
relevance: Shapes the Cartographer state-ACI command surface around the loop's milestones.

title: Four validation layers even with an ACI
claim: Keep JSON Schema even with an ACI, in layers: (1) JSON Schema (shape: missing fields, bad enums, malformed timestamps), (2) invariant checks (cross-file logic: current_phase_id exists in plan.json, next_action_id is active, completed task has a receipt, no forbidden path in write set, receipt references existing log), (3) ACI commands (allowed transitions), (4) Git diffs / human review (observability).
evidence: S009 'Keep JSON Schema even with an ACI': the four layers and the schema-vs-invariant catch lists.
relevance: Defines the validation stack the state-management tooling implements.

title: Cartographer implementation: file truth, ACI writes, escape hatch
claim: Use file-backed state as source of truth but mutate it through cartographer commands. Direct file edits are allowed only for proposal.md, ADRs, and generated/human docs. Harness rule: the agent may read .cartographer/*.json and *.jsonl directly, must not directly edit canonical state files unless the ACI is unavailable, and after any direct edit must run cartographer state validate.
evidence: S009 'How I'd implement this in Pi-Cartographer': canonical/preferred-mutation/escape-hatch layout and the three harness rules.
relevance: Concrete integration plan plus a resilience escape hatch so the ACI is not a single point of failure.

title: Rule of thumb: validated transitions over observable files
claim: Raw files for truth, ACIs for transitions, schemas for shape, invariant checks for meaning, JSONL for evidence: the best state-management interface is an ACI that performs validated state transitions over plain, observable JSON/JSONL files.
evidence: S009 'Concrete rule of thumb' and final one-sentence summary.
relevance: One-line statement of the target architecture for the proposal.

title: Hybrid state interface: file read path + ACI write path
claim: Canonical agent state must be observable JSON/JSONL files that the agent reads directly, but mutations must go through a semantic state-transition ACI that validates schema + cross-file invariants and appends JSONL evidence; direct canonical-state edits are an escape hatch only when the ACI is unavailable and must be followed by re-validation.
evidence: S009 (hybrid model and harness rules) plus S017 (ACI improves agent performance).
relevance: Binds the proposal's state design to observable-files + controlled-writes rather than raw editing or an opaque store.

title: ACI as single point of failure / overengineering
claim: An ACI introduces its own risks: tool bugs become state bugs, opaque tools are harder to recover from, the agent can become dependent on behavior it cannot inspect, and the interface can be overengineered.
evidence: S009 ACI-only tradeoff 'Cons': 'tool bugs become state bugs... harder to recover if opaque... risk of overengineering... agent may become dependent on tool behavior it cannot inspect.'
relevance: Mitigated by the hybrid model: observable raw files, schema/invariant validation runnable outside the harness, and a direct-edit escape hatch with re-validation [F086][F090].
